draft.title: The Cold War
card: The Cold War was a long rivalry after 1945 between the United States and the Soviet Union. Each was a superpower, a country with huge military and economic strength.
The two sides competed for power and influence around the world. They did not fight each other directly, which is why it was called a cold war rather than a hot one.
The United States and the Soviet Union both built nuclear weapons. Many people feared that a mistake or a crisis could start a nuclear war.
This fear shaped everyday culture. Films and songs dealt with nuclear war, and some families and schools practised what to do in an attack.
draft.remember: The Cold War was a rivalry, not a direct fight, and fear of nuclear war shaped daily life.

a.q: Why was the rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union called a cold war?
opts: They competed without fighting each other directly
They fought only in cold, snowy places
They had stopped all contact with each other
They fought a short war and then made peace
a.why: The word cold shows that the two superpowers competed for power but did not fight each other directly. The option about stopping all contact is tempting, but the rivalry was an active contest for influence around the world.
a.clue: Think about whether the two sides fought each other directly.

b.q: In the 1950s, a school in a US city holds regular drills where students practise what to do in a nuclear attack. What does this show about the Cold War?
opts: Fear of nuclear war affected daily life
Soldiers from the Soviet Union had landed in the US
The US and the Soviet Union were at war directly
Schools were run by the military during the Cold War
b.why: The drills show that fear of nuclear war reached into ordinary life, even for students. They do not show direct fighting, because the Cold War was a rivalry without the two superpowers fighting each other.
b.clue: Ask what the drills say about how people felt, not about any fighting.

a.best: They competed without fighting each other directly

b.best: Fear of nuclear war affected daily life
